title: Repair PR 784 identity seam
objective: Repair the two open identity-seam findings on PR 784 and publish them onto that same open PR. I784-01 must reject a same-revision projection whose bytes do not match the receipt digest before an assertion is signed, by reusing one pure verifier already implied by the governance checker. I784-02 must stop an OAuth client string from denying a registered adapter actor, while a client string alone still selects no actor and never enters provenance. I784-U01 stays an owner interpretation: do not change result=resolved or invent a ReleaseIdentity. GAR: architecture is already settled (canonical projection plus runtime assertion issuer); the intervention reuses the existing output-digest check rather than a new identity design. Publication target is the already-checked-out branch feat/memory-native-http-consumer (head 4e5e5a0cf0f5dc82fbbf0f1b356b38430d9e6107), which is PR 784 against main. Do not cut a sibling branch and do not retarget the base.
success_criteria: A same-revision projection whose actor description changes and whose receipt is untouched is refused before seal_identity_assertion, while the unchanged canonical fixture still mints

disconfirming_questions: Does hashing the file still pass when the committed projection and receipt already agree, or does the happy path now refuse every mint?
Does removing the OAuth equality test let a client id that is not manus, codex, or gemini become an actor?
Does a status check fire only after the digest matches, so a content tamper cannot be laundered as a current actor?
Would publishing with PR_STACK=auto retarget PR 784 onto a sibling chain instead of updating it against main?
assumed_false_ifs: The receipt digest is assumed to be the projection hash. It is only a claim until the file bytes are hashed.
OAuth equality is assumed to be an authorization control. It denies a registered adapter and is invisible to the evidence digest.
result=resolved is assumed to mean every applicable dimension is known. The audit says that reading is unresolved and the Memory 2.6.0 verifier requires resolved.
